text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-A five-nation group monitoring ceasefire in Lebanon will discuss an Israeli complaint filed on Friday after an Israeli soldier was killed in a Hizbollah guerrilla attack in Israel's south Lebanon Occupation zone.
-French Foreign Minister De Charette arrives in Beirut on Thursday on a short official visit.
-Bank of Lebanon's gross foreign exchange reserves rose by $90.27 million at end of February to $6,261.37 million in mid-February.
-Acting Finance Minister Siniora left to Brussels to discuss Lebanon's joining of the European-Mediterranean partnership.
-Israeli planes raided suspected Hizbollah positions in south Lebanon.
-A Japanese government envoy will meet President Hrawi and Prime Minister Hariri to discuss the issue of the suspected Red Army members held in Lebanon.
-Parliament Speaker Berri headed to Kuwait on a three-day official visit.
